neighbours.label: the word just before an expected 'data' or 'output' in I/O and buffering contexts (more, extra, pending, remaining)
fire: The parser keeps reading until no more data arrives on the pipe.
Any extra bytes beyond the limit are silently dropped by the driver.
The loop sleeps briefly when the socket has no new data to read.
Calling flush forces any buffered output to be written to the file.
The client waits for incoming data before sending a reply.
If the stream ends early, the remaining data is lost.
The callback fires whenever the device produces more samples.
Old log entries are trimmed when the disk fills with excess data.
quiet: The guard keeps watching until no more cars arrive at the gate.
Any extra guests beyond the limit are politely turned away at the door.
The cat sleeps briefly when the house has no new visitors to greet.
Calling early forces the doctor to see the patient before lunch.
The host waits for incoming guests before serving dinner.
If the game ends early, the remaining tickets are refunded.
The bell rings whenever the bakery produces more bread.
Old shoes are donated when the closet fills with excess clutter.

notes: Top: 'waits for', 'produces more', 'Waiting for more', 'extra', 'pending' in code/docstrings; output promotes data/Data/_data. Probe: more .21, extra .18, pending .17 vs non-I/O .002.
